[00:00] Maya: okay hi everybody, thanks for making time, um we've got about 40 minutes, so we'll run through current renewal position and then Carlos will pick up on the latency/burst questions.
[00:12] Priya: thanks, Maya; quick context: we're broadly happy with the platform, we just need to model out cost and latency if we add APAC region and bump capacity by about 2.5x. also need clarity on private vpc/onprem pilot for regulatory teams.
[00:28] Carlos: great, yeah hi i'm Carlos, i'm the solutions eng on this. for the latency piece, the main knobs are routing policy, model variant and regional capacity. we can do hosted APAC or dedicated in ap-east, or a private onprem that we verified — each has different perf/cost.
[00:45] David: quick q, last time we saw spurty p99 spikes during peak — are those KV cache misses or batch sizing? i think it's both.
[00:56] Anya: yeah, our SRE saw big jumps when seq length went longer for summarization flows. We send a lot of 2-3k tokens sometimes.
[01:08] Carlos: okay that helps. large seqs definitely change kernel selection in the runtime; there are also prefix caching considerations. we often recommend aggressive KV/prefix caching plus smaller continuous batches for low tail latency.
[01:22] Priya: when you say private onprem ",onpre.." i didn't catch — is that fully airgapped or VPC-hosted? what do our security teams expect?
[01:31] Maya: good q — two options: Redwood Private (VPC with customer-managed networking) or the onprem package for airgapped installs. Private has the same control plane but customer-provided networking; onprem is an installed bundle — needs more lead time and an ops handoff.
[01:48] David: lead time, how long?
[01:50] Carlos: typical onprem pilot is 8-12 weeks for staging + certs; VPC-style private is more like 3-5 weeks depending on infra and access to KMS.
[02:03] Priya: KMS — we need HSM-backed keys for certain datasets. do you support HSM integrations?
[02:10] Maya: yes we have KMS/HSM integrations, there are notes in our security pack; we'll share the doc. we integrate with common cloud KMS providers and can support external HSMs via the keystore adaptor.
[02:21] Anya: and audit logs? we need immutable audit trail for model access and tokenized logs redaction.
[02:29] Carlos: audit logs are supported, and we have token-level cost and latency breakdowns from the console. redaction and retention policies can be configured; we'll share the retention matrix.
[02:40] David: pricing — if we do 2.5x reserved capacity plus APAC region, what's the uplift percentage ballpark?
[02:48] Maya: ballpark — APAC region + dedicated nodes is usually a 15-25% uplift depending on instance class and network egress; reserved commit reduces unit price. burst capacity and canary policies also affect list vs committed rates. we'll send a detailed fit/quote.
[03:03] Priya: is there a way to route lower priority traffic to cheaper model variants automatically?
[03:08] Carlos: yes, smart routing policies can route by latency vs cost tiers, fallback to quantized or distilled variants; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles by workload. ps note: the transcript sometimes shows the product as everwood or redwood, ignore that — it's redwood.
[03:23] Anya: for the bench, we want a realistic baseline — can you run a sim that mirrors our mix: 60% short prompts (<=200 tokens), 30% mid (200-800), 10% long (800-3000)? and show p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens?
[03:36] Carlos: yep we can do that. we'll run a bench using the same seq distribution, and include KV cache hit/miss scenarios. expect spreadsheet with cost calc and latency columns.
[03:45] Priya: timeline — we need internal approvals by Jan 20 to get procurement started for Feb rollout.
[03:51] Maya: understood. we'll prioritize the quote and bench so you have materials.
[03:56] David: any lock-in risks if we go with Dedicated reserved nodes vs hosted API?
[04:02] Carlos: minimal lock-in — same API surface, you can pin model versions and use routing policies. Dedicated gives you isolation but you'll have to coordinate kernel/optimization rollouts with ops schedule. fallback policies can route to hosted if capacity hits limit.
[04:18] Priya: competitor question — our procurement flagged AivenAI as cheaper for EU/cheap team trials, how do you compare?
[04:25] Maya: many vendors price different slices; our differentiation is the production-first tooling, transparent latency/cost breakdowns and the unified runtime. we'll provide a comparison sheet; also note total cost of ops vs just list price matters.
[04:38] Anya: thought — for private pilot we need a small onprem PoC (2 nodes) to validate p99 at our seq distributions. what's the minimum commit?
[04:47] Carlos: for a pilot we can support a small onprem POD without heavy commit; commercial terms vary but we can scope a 3-month pilot with reduced fees, then roll into reserved commit on success.
[04:58] Priya: ok great. can we get the SOC2 and ISO reports now? security will want them attached to the procurement packet.
[05:05] Maya: yes. i'll put them in the shared drive; i'll also include our KMS integration notes and an ops checklist.
[05:12] David: one nit — last time your console mis-attributed a route in our logs, i want to make sure the tracing hooks are per-route and token-level.
[05:21] Carlos: tracing is per-route and we have hooks for custom trace ids. i'll include an example tracing config.
[05:27] Priya: sounds good. timeline recap? we need quote + bench by Jan 12 ideally, approvals by Jan 20.
[05:34] Maya: yes, quote + bench by Jan 12 (we'll try to accelerate), follow-up demo deep-dive Jan 14, procurement readout Jan 20.
[05:42] David: all right thanks.
